R327 — actual native head and dense format ledger
Date: 2026-10-13
Source: W worktree `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/perf-native-copy-cohorts-qualified-20261012`, task pin e3c904e2 (parent-provided).
Model path supplied by Main: `/home/yayoi/.local/share/strata-sycl/models/qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s/IQ3_S/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf`.

Finding

The actual loaded GGUF types and dense override histogram are still absent from the available closed evidence. Do not infer output.weight type from the IQ3_S pack/model label or the pack index. R325's conditional IQ4_XS example therefore remains hypothetical.

Evidence reviewed

- R325 report (closed): `research-free-decode-dense-head-kernel-criticalpath-round325-v1.txt`. It says the serve verifier's one-token route does mixer → Q8_1 quantization → native_mmvq for output.weight, and that neither selected head type nor current dense histogram was recorded. It explicitly excludes NativeHead::run's separate Q5_K shortcut from the verifier path.
- Closed B70 MMVQ fixture: `bench/results/2026-09-30-xe-mmvq-speed/README.md`. It measures synthetic IQ4_XS head weights, not the supplied B570 model's selected type. It cannot close the missing B570 evidence.
- Current registry summary: `bench/results/2026-10-13-model-comparison-policy/REPORT.md` contains controller and qualification summaries, not actual tensor-type details. No closed README matched the selected loader output or a per-tensor dense histogram. I did not read live Main logs or active receipts.
- Static pack metadata: `packs/qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s/index.txt` identifies itself as generated by `tools/iq_pack.py` and lists 1,079 pack tensors. The line for `output.weight` has zero pack offsets and dimensions 2560×248320 with trailing fields including 8 and 32; these are pack-index fields, not an authenticated GGUF type for the native output head. `native_experts.txt` records expert-layer types and byte offsets only. There is no `dense.txt` in this pack directory. The header's model filename is provenance, not a type ledger.
- Pinned W source: `src/core/native_head.cpp:35-46` opens the GGUF model and selects `output.weight`, validates supported type and shape [2560,248320], then computes bytes from its actual type. Lines 66-83 may rewrite GGML Q6_K (14) or Q8_0 (8) to native row layouts, so record both original GGUF type and post-conversion native type.
- Pinned W source: `src/core/native_dense.cpp:48-59` defines eligible native-dense tensor names: suffixes `.attn_qkv.weight`, `.attn_gate.weight`, `.ssm_out.weight`, `.attn_q.weight`, `.attn_k.weight`, `.attn_v.weight`, `.attn_output.weight`, `.ffn_gate_shexp.weight`, `.ffn_up_shexp.weight`, and `.ffn_down_shexp.weight`; plus `blk.1.ple_key.weight` only when enabled and its type is one of 42, 18, 23, or 8. Lines 187-248 filter unsupported types/shapes, enforce the canonical matrix shape, upload weights, and convert eligible Q6_K/Q8_0 storage to row layouts. The actual attached set depends on the supplied GGUF shards, current layer range, PLE setting, support table, and successful load. Do not assume every eligible name was attached.

Safe follow-up after Main's active job closes

Use a header-only read that calls the existing `strata::GgufModel::open(model_path)` / `GgufFile` metadata interface and prints each selected tensor's name, original `TensorInfo.type`, full shape, containing shard number/path, and calculated `native_mmvq_weight_bytes(type, ne0, ne1)`. The reader must only inspect GGUF metadata (`tensors()`, `find()`, `shape`, `type`, split metadata); it must not call `tensor_data()`, map/read tensor payloads intentionally, allocate device memory, or initialize SYCL. Open the model from the first shard through `GgufModel::open` so the shard containing output.weight is resolved correctly.

Required exact query:
1. `output.weight`.
2. Every present matrix in every shard whose name matches the exact suffixes above, plus the exact optional name `blk.1.ple_key.weight`; print all eligible matrices first, then separately mark which would pass `native_mmvq_supported(type)`, shape rank 2 and the runtime layer-range/PLE gates. For the current free one-token head/dense ledger, layer ranges and PLE enablement should come from the just-closed run's own public summary; record `STRATA_HC_Q8` separately because it selects alternate HC weights, not the regular native-dense suffix set.
3. Also report the full set of loaded `NativeDense::served_names` if a closed, matching runtime receipt exposes it. If no such receipt exists, a header-only eligible set is not proof of attached/runtime-selected weights.

The safe standalone implementation should use `GgufModel::open` and metadata fields only; conceptually:
```cpp
auto model = strata::GgufModel::open(argv[1]);
for (const auto& tensor : all_model_tensors(model)) {
  if (tensor.name == "output.weight" || native_dense_name_matches(tensor.name))
    print(tensor.name, tensor.type, tensor.shape, containing_shard(tensor));
}
```
Do not substitute an implementation that calls `tensor_data`; NativeHead/NativeDense loaders do so for upload. After metadata is available, compare these rows to the just-closed loader's loaded/attached count and record original GGML types separately from converted native layout IDs.

Conclusion

R325's next kernel comparison remains ungrounded until this type ledger and the actual attached dense set are recorded from the closed run. No selected-type speed claim, type-specific candidate, or B570 performance estimate is made here. No model payload, build, parser, device, GPU run, or active receipt was read or executed for this report.
